SLAM's own order of operations. A step can declare a prerequisite step (reached first: every step before it that counts is done) and conditions on the numbers. A locked step shows a lock and its plain reason, is never where you are, and never counts as a hole. Unlock anyway needs a note (kept on the session record) and shows the cost in FI days a year, coach only.
Spend on what you love (Joy Basics · Pick the few things worth spending on): the joy lines (goals and mindset live here too)

Spend on what you love: Joy Basics · Pick the few things worth spending on. Fund the few things that make daily life good. Problem: Budgets that cut everything feel like punishment, and people quit. Unlocks: A plan that doesn't feel like a diet Done when: The joy lines are picked and funded.

Stop going backwards (Stop the Bleeding · Spend less than you make; little e = $1,000 or your highest deductible, whichever is smaller): no late bills, payday debt at $0, little e full, income gaps within 12 months covered

Stop going backwards: Stop the Bleeding · Spend less than you make; little e = $1,000 or your highest deductible, whichever is smaller. Bills current, no payday debt, little e full, income gaps covered. Problem: One surprise turns into late fees and new debt. Unlocks: Small surprises stop turning into new debt Done when: No late bill, payday debt at $0, little e full, any gap within 12 months covered.
Get the full match (Free Money · Contribute enough to get every dollar of the employer match): the full employer match

Get the full match: Free Money · Contribute enough to get every dollar of the employer match. Get the full employer match. Problem: Leaving an instant 50 to 100% return on the table. Unlocks: An instant 50 to 100% return Done when: Putting in enough to get the whole match (or no match is offered).

Pay off high-interest debt (Heavy Debt · Every debt at 8% or more, surplus first): cards, payday, personal, medical, BNPL, or any APR at or over the heavy line (8%); the surplus goes here first while any is carried (the debt rule)

Pay off high-interest debt: Heavy Debt · Every debt at 8% or more, surplus first. Pay off everything at 8% or more, with the surplus going there first. Problem: Interest working against you faster than investing works for you. Unlocks: That interest stops, and those payments become yours Done when: No debt at or over the heavy line.
Build your job-loss fund (big e · Your age divided by 5 months of spending): the Rule of 5, FAT first, then DRAFTT, then full spending

Build your job-loss fund: big e · Your age divided by 5 months of spending. Your age divided by 5 is the months of spending saved. Problem: A job loss forcing new debt or selling investments at a bad time. Unlocks: A job loss is a plan, not a panic Done when: Every big e layer (FAT, DRAFTT, full) is full.

Max out tax-free accounts: Tax-Free Growth · Roth IRA and HSA, to the limit. Max the Roth IRA and the HSA. Problem: Paying tax on decades of growth. Unlocks: Money that grows and comes out tax-free Done when: The Roth IRA (and the HSA, when eligible) is maxed for the year.

Two numbers, asked together on Home at the start of every session in one small prompt, one answer per person in a couple, kept per session, stored in every snapshot, charted from Day 0 on Home as a slim pair, and rows on Day 0 vs now (answer 164). Confidence (the meta measure, the old money feeling): 'How confident (vs afraid) do you feel about your money?' (1 afraid to 10 confident); it rates the Mindset area and drives the debt method suggestion. Joy (the local measure): 'How much joy do you get from your money?' (1 little joy to 10 full of joy); it pairs with the category joy ratings on the Budget. An older file's money feeling imports as Confidence.

Data kept in the client file for a later Wrapped or Kanban, with the least UI: a dated joy rating (1 to 5) per spending category (Budget › Joy by category); a Trip tag on Budget lines and calendar entries; an income type on each income row (Salary, Side hustle, Windfall, Other; blank reads from the row's type); and a change log on every edit with the field, the old and new value, who (Coach, or Client when Client view is on) and the time. All of it exports and imports with the file; the Captured tab of the workbook lists it.
